name: Arduino UNO R3

buses.i2c: SDA A4 / SCL A5 (there's another SDA/SCL pair next to AREF at the top-left of the board; it's the same wires as A4/A5)
buses.spi: SCK 13 / MISO 12 / MOSI 11 / SS 10 (also duplicated on the ICSP header)
buses.uart: Serial: TX 1 / RX 0, wired to the onboard USB-serial chip, so you see output as soon as you plug in USB. This is the only hardware UART; for a Bluetooth module use SoftwareSerial or give up pins 0/1

power: 5V logic! I/O outputs 5V and expects 5V on inputs. Max 40mA per pin (stay under 20mA), and no more than 200mA total across all I/O. The 3.3V header pin gives only 50mA: enough for an OLED, not much else. VIN / the DC jack take 7-12V. On USB power the 5V pin can supply peripherals about 400mA
flash_how: One USB-B cable (the square 'printer' connector) to your computer, then pio run -t upload flashes directly. Official boards use an ATmega16U2 USB chip that needs no driver on Mac; most clones use a CH340, which may need the CH340 driver on older macOS and Windows. The board auto-resets before flashing; no buttons to press. The TX/RX LEDs blink rapidly while flashing. Serial monitor: pio device monitor, with the baud rate matching Serial.begin in your code
gotchas: The UNO is 5V logic; STM32, ESP32 and most OLED/SD-card modules are 3.3V. Connecting UNO outputs directly to them can fry them, while 3.3V signals into the UNO are usually (barely) recognized. Use a level shifter when mixing
D0/D1 are the USB serial pins. If your program uses Serial, don't connect anything to these two; anything attached during flashing also makes the upload fail
Only D2 (INT0) and D3 (INT1) support external interrupts; attachInterrupt doesn't work on other pins (PCINT is a separate story)
tone() uses Timer2 and breaks analogWrite on D3 and D11
The Servo library uses Timer1 and breaks analogWrite on D9 and D10

Only 2KB of RAM. String concatenation, big arrays and U8g2 full-buffer mode (128x64 alone needs 1KB) easily exhaust memory and cause bizarre resets. Wrap serial string literals in the F("...") macro to keep them in Flash
Once you use I2C (Wire), A4/A5 can no longer read analog values
D13 is both the onboard LED and the SPI clock; the LED flickers during SPI, which is normal
The ADC is 10-bit (0-1023) with a default 5V reference, so one step is about 4.9mV
There are no STM32-style pin names (PA0); everything is numbers. Writing 13 or A0 works directly in PlatformIO
The CH340 on clone UNOs shows up on your computer as wchusbserial or COMx; if it isn't detected, install the driver first
